question:
What position are you hiring for? Please give me:
- Job title
- Brief description of the role (2-3 sentences)
- Full-time, part-time, or contract?

What are the requirements for this role?

Please list:
- **Must-haves** (dealbreakers — candidates without these get rejected)
- **Nice-to-haves** (preferred but not required)

Example:
Must-haves: 2+ years barista experience, available weekends
Nice-to-haves: latte art, food handler certification

What is the compensation for this role? (hourly rate, salary, or range)

This helps me answer candidate questions about pay. If you'd prefer not to share this publicly, just say 'competitive' and I'll use that.

When are you available for interviews? Please give me your recurring weekly availability.

Example:
- Tuesdays 2pm–5pm
- Thursdays 10am–12pm

I'll offer these slots to candidates I invite to interview.

How do you want to run interviews?
- In-person (if so, what address?)
- Phone call
- Video call (Zoom, Google Meet, etc.)
- Combination

Also: how long should each interview be? (e.g. 30 minutes, 1 hour)

How do you want me to handle rejections?
- Send a brief, standard rejection to everyone who doesn't move forward
- Only send rejections after the interview stage (earlier candidates just get no response)
- Send personalized rejections with brief feedback

I recommend option 1 — it's professional and candidates appreciate the closure.

Do you want me to conduct reference checks before making an offer?
- Yes — I'll contact references provided by the candidate
- No — skip reference checks
- Only for finalists (last 1-2 candidates)
When should I ask you to approve emails before sending them to candidates?

options.label: Always — I want to review every email before it goes out
For all candidate emails (recommended for hiring)
Only for risky messages (offers, rejections after interview)

question: Anything else I should know about this role or your hiring process? Any specific questions you want me to ask candidates, deal-breakers I haven't listed, or anything about your company culture worth mentioning in communications?
